Yup. That's what this story is going to be about. Getting lost and gettin' in a ditch. I'm the main character of this story!

So my(former) job took me to different home depot/Lowes. This was the first real job I had which took me to areas I was completely unfamiliar with in the biggest city in Texas.

After finishing my FIRST day on the job, I make my way to my classes after work. I take a wrong turn then end up on Highway 90 alternate in my dunky little car that shakes violently going over 75.(hint, if you're not going 90mph on a Texas highway, you're slowing everyone else down). So, this cars gas gauge is completely unreliable after the tank goes under a quarter tank which is where my meter was pointing, and i'm out in nothing but cornfields and I actually hit the end of this damn highway. After calling a parent, panicking asking for directions, I pull into a parking lot of an Ice House to calm down and figure out the last bit of my route. I try to back out and BAM! I'm in a ditch the EXACT size of my car. 3 cowboys come out from the ice house to save me. All on my first day of work!

BONUS: i was just around the corner from my destination!

After a long 3 months of preparation, and only a heart attack's worth of stress, it's finally here...the Anime Summit Podcast!

Welcome, boys and girls, Onii-chans and Onee-san!

Three months ago I started putting together this podcast project. After some bumpy starts I recorded multiple practice sessions alone, and pitched them out to members of the /r/anime community. I got lots of good feedback, but finding co-hosts was difficult. Eventually I wrangled in 3 such co-hosts and we got to recording more practices. At one point, we were recording 2 practice sessions a week as we upgraded our equipment and got more familiar with our software, and each other.

We managed to get a hold of some very talented artists and designers to give us our amazing Mascot character. We still don't have a name for her, but I think we may go with Kaylee-chan. Tell us what you think in the comments!

They also gave us the wonderful logo, featuring our mascot up front! Hopefully in the future we can get awesome artwork done of her in various topical anime outfits (Boobstring, anyone?)

But, here we are, launching with 5 episode ready for you to indulge in. Our aim is to keep our podcast under 1 hour and release 1 episode a week, every Monday! So now your drive to work on Monday mornings will be more entertaining, and you can keep thinking about your Waifu instead of your boss!

This post will be a short guide to these 5 available shows, as well as information on keeping up to date with the show and listening to it on your favorite device!

Twitter

You can follow us on Twitter @AnimeSummit to be kept abreast of new episodes, and other anime news we think you'll enjoy!

iTunes

For Apple users (and really confused android users) we have iTunes! Simply subscribe and listen at your leisure! https://itunes.apple.com/us/podcast/anime-summit/id1018790874 (Additionally, if you like the show, subscribing on itunes, even if you don't intend to really listen all the time does a lot to help us out through this launch. Thanks!)

RSS Feed

For those with their favorite podcast apps, or able to figure it out, you can find our RSS feed here: http://ranime.libsyn.com/rss At this time, we don't have any details on any apps that have us in their directory, but pretty much all podcast apps have an option for 'add from RSS'. Just plug that baby in and hit refresh every monday morning! I recommend Podcast Addict on the Play Store

In Browser

For those a little simpler, or unwilling to make the serious commitment of subscribing, just click the direct link. Modern smartphones should be smart enough to figure out how to play the MP3s and modern browsers will handle it just fine as well!

Now onto the Content!

Clicking the header link will take you to our pretty post on our website that contains show notes to give you a better idea of what to expect.

Episode 01: Introductions and Favorites

Direct link: http://traffic.libsyn.com/ranime/Anime_Summit_Ep01.mp3

Here you'll get be introduced to our hosts, and learn about some of our favorite shows! Beware, there may be some small spoilers for some of the shows, especially if they're a bit older. We make a strong effort to avoid major spoilers, but trying to keep too much covered means we'd have nothing to talk about.

Episode 02: Spring 2015 Anime Season

Direct link: http://traffic.libsyn.com/ranime/Anime_Summit_Ep02.mp3

We're back again to talk about some of our favorite shows from the Spring Season (about 11 episodes in at recording) and how we feel about them. Be prepared for Food Fights, and Band Camp! There may be small spoilers, but we've done our best to mainly discuss themes, and characters, and not major story moments! Enjoy!

Episode 03: Rating Systems and Genres

Direct Link: http://traffic.libsyn.com/ranime/Anime_Summit_Ep03.mp3

What do rating systems mean to you? Do you score off pure artistic merit? Enjoyment? Recommend-ability? Does a 10 mean you tell your mom? Our hosts explain how they rate shows, and what numbers mean what to them. On top of that, they also discuss the merits of gore in shows, and what genres they've grown to love!

Episode 04: Anime Reviews Batch 01

Direct Link: http://traffic.libsyn.com/ranime/Anime_Summit_Ep04.mp3

Every host was given the homework to find a show no more than one other host has seen, watch it, and prepare a little presentation on the show. The shows picked span the last 3 decades of anime! Who will come out on top?!

Episode 05: Tropes, Sequels, Prequels, and Spinoffs

Direct Link: http://traffic.libsyn.com/ranime/Anime_Summit_Ep05.mp3

Within these halls we talk about our recent experiences at Anime Expo 2015 and Convergence Minnesota. We also discuss our favorite tropes and those that really turn us off from watching a show. Eventually we get to talking about Sequels we dislike and those we wish existed, like K-On! University (Please?!?!)

Hopefully you enjoy our podcast! Please feel free to sing songs of our greatness, or tell us where we royally screwed up and where we can get better!

Because I do. My father-in-law. Great guy. Gentle spirit. 56 years old. I was with him when he gurgled his last breath in the ICU after his heart attack (after the previous double bypass) following his COPD diagnosis, etc. etc. It was fucking awful.

I say this because people checking out these threads might be thinking that the posters are motivated by blind hate, or are just human garbage in their daily lives. They might think they're disguising their instinctive contempt by hollow cries to improve fatties health, or to set good examples for their piglets.

Yeah, maybe. But something tells me others are here because they've buried a fatty or two in their past and know what a useless nightmare the whole ordeal is. I read the exemplary post by /u/SkinnyTwig and just had to add my own here.

My father-in-law was obese. He died trying to inflate his withered lungs under a crushing slab of porkfat while his family gathered around in confusion. To honor his memory the next day, they gathered at his favorite restaurant (overpriced tacky steak chain) and ordered his usual. They toasted him with glasses of beatus juice raised. On the one month anniversary of his passing, they gathered again and ordered his typical lunch at the local McFats: two double quarter-pounders. To the family's credit, two of them threw it up that evening and speculated that the burgers were bad. No one could comprehend that eating ONE was only marginally acceptable for a human's diet. Eating two, every day at work, month after month, was an easy way to fill the hole next to him in the graveyard.

I'm not fat. Never have been. I'm 5'10'' and 160 pounds. After saying my goodbyes to him in the hospital I drove to the gym to renew my membership I'd let lapse a few years earlier. When my time comes, I don't know how I'm going but I refuse to go like him.

So tell me FPH, anyone here buried a butterhuffer?
Know a Fatty who has gone through the Golden Arches in the sky? Tell me about them!

I might soon. One side of my family is naturally big, as in height and weight (not obese, just chubby). One aunt has struggled with her weight in an extreme way, but I never thought she'd get go the point of obesity.

The woman lives in Taiwan with most of my family, so fatties aren't exactly super common, rich or poor. Yet last month I'm told she needs an oxygen mask when she sleeps or she'll stop breathing; haven't seen my recent pictures of her, but I'm told her weight has gotten bad.

She's a nice woman, if a bit pushy. Never had good taste in food, but she definitely enjoyed eating. Her husband and two kids aren't at all fat, and they'll likely be burying my aunt soon enough.

Depresses the shit out of me.

My dad's sister-in-law was the hugest person I'd ever seen when I was a young child. For all intents and purposes she was nice enough, but she was so fat she would just sit on the couch and call her children over to her to have them gopher stuff for her. I never really saw her not sitting down. Never saw her actually play with her children. I suppose it's sad if you think about it long enough, but obviously she brought it on herself. I'm not very close with that side of the family, and when I heard she had died a couple weeks after she'd been buried, I felt no remorse. I was surprised she lasted as long as she did.
I genuinely just hate fat people on first sight. Not sure why everyone says they don't believe that of us. This is FPH
I find the Ham HAES stuff irrelevant, even if their delusions were true. My hate is based on aesthetics.

One of my closest friends, in '03, from a heart attack. He was 37. Good fucking christ, the life he has missed since then. His eyes were to the sky, and I was COMPLETELY freaked. I kinda took charge and told this girl to grab his other arm and we are going to drag him to a flat spot. And now I can't write about it anymore.

The thing that was missing from IRC was a good authentication / login system.

Find an IRC daemon and add so that it authenticates vs Voat's userbase.

IRC was designed to be distributed, work on low power systems. We used to run irc daemons on Pentium 100s with 48GB of RAM and it would support thousands of users. Toss up 5-10 VPSs across the world, link them on the same network.

I would donate a VPS or self hosted server for irc##.voat.co (and if my server is shit, drop it from the round robin and don't let me connect. I'd rather do that than buy "gold" or click on ads.

You could even set up a 1:1 mapping between Ops and Mods. /v/___ would have a corresponding #___. channel. There are a lot of channel modes to control about any aspect of chat that you wanted.

There are multiple bots that add features to channels. For example you could even add another "Chat Karma" field for Voat so people could accumulate 'karma' on Chat. #theredpill's IRC bot and #TrollChromosomes's IRC bot are actually pretty good.

There's no reason to reinvent the wheel when it comes to Chat. IRC is was pretty good and worked on a huge range of systems. And now there are web (like irccloud.com), phone and standalone clients.
